assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Motherson Sumi Wiring India (standalone; no subsidiaries; Rs crore). One business (wiring harnesses and harness components for Indian vehicle makers), so revenue grows at a single rate and EBITDA margin is a driver; the business-line build (existing plants vs the three greenfields) is kept in lineBuild and checked against model revenue in MSUMI.ctx.js. Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: FY27: Q1 revenue Rs3,407 cr (+37%; ~7 points copper pass-through, the rest volume, content and new programmes); Q1 x4 is already +19%. We assume Rs3,550 cr in each of Q2 and Q3 and ~Rs3,600 cr in Q4 (growth falls to ~8% in Q4 against a Rs3,335 cr base that already carried copper and the greenfields). FY28-29: PV production +6-8% a year (after the GST-cut year), content per vehicle +4-5% (features, EV/hybrid share 8.5% of revenue in Q1FY27, 1.5-1.7x the content of an ICE car per JM Financial), greenfields reaching ~Rs2,000 cr a year; copper held at Q1FY27 levels (no further pass-through inflation).

lineBuild._why: Company disclosure: FY26 revenue Rs11,478 cr = existing plants Rs10,438 cr + greenfields Rs1,040 cr (Q4FY26 presentation p10). Greenfields ran at ~Rs443-450 cr a quarter in Q4FY26-Q1FY27 and are sized for ~Rs2,000 cr a year (Q4FY26 call). Existing plants are the balance.

assumptions._marginWhy: FY26 9.2% (11.4% excluding Rs127 cr of greenfield start-up losses); Q1FY27 7.6%. FY27: Q1 7.6%, then ~8.5% for Q2-Q4 as the 3-6 month copper lag unwinds (management: majority of customers on a three-month reset) and the greenfields move above breakeven, but the NCR minimum-wage increase (35-40%) is recovered only partly and slowly ('nobody can predict exactly the timeline'). FY28-29: greenfields at parity with old plants and some wage recovery; we stay well below the 11-13% of FY22-25 because copper pass-through at cost permanently inflates revenue (denominator effect, as the CFO said) and royalty, management fee and support fees to the two partners take ~2.4% of revenue.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex guided at ~Rs200 cr in FY27 (Q4FY26 call), funded internally; FY26 Rs201 cr. Management said in Aug-2026 that new expansion plans will follow 'in the next few quarters' as plants run at ~80%. We add ~Rs40 cr a year of new leased plant (right-of-use assets, most plants are leased from SAMIL) because the engine has no lease line, and lift capex to Rs270-280 cr in FY28-29 for the next round of plants.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs216 cr = 13.5% of average gross block (Rs1,604 cr), high because right-of-use (leased) buildings and harness tooling depreciate fast. Q1FY27 Rs60 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to net cash only (borrowings include Rs223 cr of lease liabilities, so there is no treasury income until net cash turns positive). Bank deposit yield ~6%.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Recurring items, not treasury: interest unwinding on security deposits with SAMIL and others (Rs2.7 cr in FY26, AR note 31), interest on deposits and small asset-sale gains. FY26 other income Rs3.9 cr (AR note 22; Rs12.8 cr in FY25 when cash was higher); Q1FY27 Rs5.4 cr. FY27E = Q1 plus ~Rs1.2 cr a quarter; Rs6 cr from FY28.
assumptions._interestWhy: Mostly interest on lease liabilities (Rs20.5 cr in FY26 incl. leases from SAMIL) plus working-capital lines: external debt rose from Rs10 cr (Mar-26) to Rs61 cr (Jun-26); Q1FY27 finance cost Rs8 cr.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Policy-like payout of ~62% of profit for FY26 (final Rs0.58 a share) and FY25; 59-65% since listing.

cover.headline: India's wiring-harness leader on a trough multiple: the margin squeeze is mostly timing, the JV toll is permanent
cover.lead: Motherson Sumi Wiring India (MSWIL) assembles the wiring harnesses in most Indian cars; it is a joint venture of Samvardhana Motherson (33.4%) and Sumitomo Wiring Systems (25.1%), and one customer (Maruti Suzuki, per Emkay) buys 41% of its output. Revenue grew 23% in FY26 and 37% in Q1FY27, but the EBITDA margin fell to 7.6% as copper ran ahead of price resets, NCR minimum wages jumped 35-40% and new plants ramped up; profit was flat. We forecast EPS of ₹1.01 / ₹1.30 / ₹1.53 for FY27-29E, below the street. The street values MSWIL on **P/E on one-year-forward EPS** (MOSL 35x and JM 33x FY28E, Emkay 30x Jun-28E). The house rule (its own forward P/E median since listing, 41.8x, cut by the 7.8% auto-component de-rating) gives **38.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹1.41 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹44; DCF ₹29, below the price. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Growth is real and well ahead of car production
arguments.p: Revenue rose 23% in FY26 against passenger-vehicle production growth of 9.4%, and 37% in Q1FY27 (30% without copper) against industry volumes of +17%. The drivers are content (more features, SUVs, EV and hybrid programmes at 8.5% of revenue and 1.5-1.7x the harness value of a petrol car) and three new plants that already sell ~₹450 cr a quarter. We model revenue +{{as.revenueGrowth.0|pct0}} / +{{as.revenueGrowth.1|pct0}} / +{{as.revenueGrowth.2|pct0}}.

arguments.h: Two of the three margin hits are temporary; the third is a negotiation
arguments.p: Copper is passed on at cost with a 3-6 month lag (the CFO put the Q4FY26 hit at 2-2.5 points of margin), and the greenfields, which lost ₹127 cr in FY26, were at breakeven excluding that lag by Q4FY26. The NCR wage increase is a real cost that customers must agree to share; there is no timeline. Copper also inflates revenue for ever, so the old 12-13% margin will not come back at today's copper price. We assume {{as.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} / {{as.ebitdaMargin.1|pct}} / {{as.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}, below every broker.

arguments.h: The JV toll: minority holders get the assembly margin
arguments.p: About 65% of raw-material purchases come from SAMIL and Sumitomo, which also take a royalty, an equal management fee and support fees: 2.4% of revenue and a quarter of EBITDA in FY26. Hyundai and Kia are served by a different SAMIL JV. Returns are still ~40% ROCE because the business needs little capital, but growth in the value chain accrues partly outside MSWIL.

arguments.h: Valuation: the price assumes the squeeze is permanent
arguments.p: At ₹34.07 the stock trades at 26.2x our FY28E and 24.1x Sep-28E EPS, against a 41.8x forward median since listing; its trailing P/E sits 27% below its median since listing while auto-component peers sit 7.8% below theirs. Our 38.5x is above the street's 30-35x because the house rule anchors on MSWIL's own history; at the street's 35x our EPS still gives ₹49. The DCF (₹29) does not support the price: the case rests on the multiple.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether the Q1 copper increase and part of the NCR wage increase have been recovered from customers, and the greenfields' first profit.
Shorter copper resets: management is asking customers for monthly (or even 15-day) price resets instead of 3-6 months; any agreement removes most of the timing squeeze.
New expansion plans "in the next few quarters" (COO, Aug-2026): new plants backed by firm orders, e.g. for customers' new car plants.
Festive-season car production (Oct-Dec 2026) against the GST-cut base; EV and hybrid launches by MSWIL's customers.
Pune and Chennai greenfields: a new customer or the delayed model launch would lift utilisation from ~50%.

sections.title: One product, one country: wiring harnesses for Indian vehicles, 64% for cars

blocks.p: A wiring harness is the bundle of wires, terminals, connectors, junction boxes, tubes and clips that carries power and signals to every electrical part of a vehicle. Each one is designed for a single model and assembled largely by hand, which makes the business labour-intensive (staff cost is 16-17% of revenue), and MSWIL places its plants next to its customers' factories. MSWIL makes them for Indian vehicle makers only (exports are negligible) in 30 plants across 16 states + 3 union territories, with 6,463 permanent employees and ~21,156 associates on the shop floor (60,000+ people including contract labour, per the company). By vehicle, FY26 revenue was 64% passenger vehicles (61% in FY25), 10% commercial vehicles, 12% two-wheelers, 6% tractors and off-road machines and 8% other (mostly components). EV programmes were 6.6% of FY26 revenue and 8.5% in Q1FY27. It supplies 9 of India's 10 best-selling car models; the exception (Hyundai and Kia) is served by a different SAMIL joint venture.

sections.title: Carved out of Motherson in 2022 to keep the Sumitomo partnership in India; two bonus issues since

blocks.p: Wiring harnesses are where the Motherson group began: Motherson Sumi Systems (MSSL) was formed with Sumitomo Wiring Systems in 1986, and the domestic harness business stayed its core as MSSL grew into a global supplier of mirrors, bumpers and modules. In 2021-22 the group reorganised. The domestic wiring-harness business (DWH) was moved into a new company, MSWIL, with an appointed date of 1-Apr-2021, and every MSSL shareholder received one MSWIL share for each MSSL share (19-Jan-2022). MSWIL listed on 28-Mar-2022. The result: Sumitomo keeps 25% of the Indian harness business directly, and SAMIL keeps 33%. Since then the share count has risen only through bonus issues (2:5 in Nov-2022, 1:2 in Jul-2025), so per-share figures are comparable once adjusted; no new money has been raised.

sections.title: Indian car production +9.4% in FY26 and a GST-led jump in Q1FY27; content per car keeps rising

blocks.p: India produced 5.54 mn passenger vehicles in FY26 (+9.4% from 5.06 mn) and 1.17 mn commercial vehicles (+13.1%), per the annual report. Lower GST rates on cars from September 2025 lifted the second half, and industry passenger-vehicle volumes rose 17% in Q1FY27. From Q3FY27 the comparison base includes the GST boost, so volume growth should slow. Harness value grows faster than volumes: SUVs keep taking share, every new model carries more electronics (screens, cameras, sensors, connected features), and electric and hybrid cars need high-voltage harnesses on top of the low-voltage ones. Copper is the swing factor: it makes up 24-28% of MSWIL's cost of goods (CFO, Q4 call) and averaged ₹1,348/kg in Q1FY27, 53% above a year earlier.

blocks.callout: **Our read:** demand is strong and content growth is structural, but MSWIL captures it as revenue more easily than as profit. The harness is an assembly business with pass-through raw materials: when copper or connectors get dearer, revenue rises and the margin percentage falls. The long-term threat, simpler zonal architectures that cut harness length, is real abroad but not yet visible in India.

bullets: **Volumes and content reach MSWIL in full.** Existing plants alone grew 15% in FY26 and 26% in Q1FY27, ahead of car production; Emkay shows MSWIL outgrowing Maruti Suzuki's volumes in every quarter.
**Part of the growth is copper.** About 5 points of Q4FY26 growth and 7 points of Q1FY27 growth were higher copper prices passed on at cost.

**Profit did not follow.** FY26 EBITDA rose 6% on 23% more revenue. The tailwind reaches MSWIL's top line; whether it reaches shareholders depends on copper resets, wage recovery and the greenfields turning profitable.

sections.title: Three new plants sell ~₹450 cr a quarter and have just reached breakeven; Pune is half empty

blocks.p: MSWIL built its first new plants since the demerger in FY25-26 to follow customers' new capacity: Kharkhoda in Haryana (combustion-engine cars, ~80% utilised), Navagam in Gujarat (EV and petrol, ~60%, a new model started in Q4FY26) and Pune (EV and petrol, ~50% because a customer postponed a launch). Two smaller sites followed: Pathredi (EV and petrol, production from Q4FY26) and Chennai (EV, volumes delayed). Together they sold ₹1,040 cr in FY26 and ~₹450 cr a quarter by Q4FY26-Q1FY27, against capacity of ~₹2,000 cr a year. Start-up losses were ₹122 cr in FY25 and ₹127 cr in FY26 (1.1 points of margin), falling to ~₹14 cr in Q4FY26. Management says the plants were at breakeven in Q4 "if you just remove the copper... lag impact" and will contribute to profit "in one or two quarters". The existing plants run at ~80%, the level at which MSWIL starts building again.

sections.title: Copper, wages and the arithmetic of pass-through: why 13% margins are not coming back

blocks.p: Three things took the EBITDA margin from 10.9% in Q1FY25 to 7.6% in Q1FY27. **Copper**: it is 24-28% of cost of goods and is passed to customers at cost, but with a lag: most customers reset prices every three months, a few every six. Copper rose from ₹883/kg in Q1FY26 to ₹1,348/kg in Q1FY27, so MSWIL kept paying today's price while billing yesterday's; the CFO put the Q4FY26 hit at "2% to 2.5% on the bottom line". Raw materials rose to 70.0% of revenue in Q4FY26 and 69.0% in Q1FY27. **Wages**: minimum wages in the NCR region, where many plants are, rose 35-40% in 2026, "much higher than what would have been anticipated"; employee cost jumped to ₹602 cr in Q1FY27 (+26.4% year on year). Recovery is "constructive discussions" with no timeline. **Greenfields**: covered in the previous chapter.

blocks.callout: **Verdict: a real but narrow moat.** MSWIL is the incumbent supplier on most of India's best-selling cars, with Sumitomo's technology and plants next to every major customer; a harness is chosen for each model, so the incumbent keeps the business for that model's life. But it has no pricing power: copper and parts are passed through, labour costs must be negotiated, and one customer takes 41% of output. Part of the value it creates is captured by its two partners. sections.title: Revenue doubled in four years; the EBITDA margin fell from 13% to 9%, so profit grew only half as fast

blocks.p: MSWIL's revenue was ₹5,635 cr in FY22, its first year as a separate company, and ₹11,478 cr in FY26: 19% a year (the demerged business had ₹3,938 cr in FY21). Net profit rose from ₹411 cr (₹457 cr before its share of the reorganisation-scheme costs) to ₹625 cr: 11% a year on the reported figure, 8% on the clean one. The difference is the margin. EBITDA was 13.0% of revenue in FY22 and 9.2% in FY26, for three reasons: copper prices rose and are passed on at cost (more revenue, no more profit); the new greenfield plants lost ₹122-127 cr a year in FY25-26 while they ramped up; and wages rose faster than the price customers pay for assembly. Depreciation doubled (₹106 cr to ₹216 cr) as new plants, mostly leased from SAMIL, came in.

blocks.p: Over FY22-26 MSWIL generated ₹2,642 cr of operating cash, spent ₹784 cr on capex and paid ₹1,283 cr of dividends (55-65% of profit). sections.title: Earnings quality: simple accounts and a clean audit; the related-party flows are the judgement call

bullets: **Simple accounts.** One company, no subsidiaries, no acquisitions, no goodwill; exceptional items only in FY22 (₹65 cr, reorganisation costs). Unmodified audit by S.R. Batliboi & Co. (EY network), whose one key audit matter is the related-party transactions.

**Cash conversion swings with copper.** Cash from operations was ₹761 cr in FY26 (122% of profit) but ₹365 cr in FY25 (60%), as receivables rose from 49 to 60 days. Payables owed to the JV partners (₹1,108 cr at Mar-2026) fund part of the inventory.

**Leases flatter EBITDA.** Most buildings are leased (₹223 cr of lease liabilities); under Ind AS 116 the ~₹115 cr a year of lease payments appears as depreciation and interest, not as an operating cost, so EBITDA is ~1 point of revenue higher than on a rent-paying basis. Peers with owned plants are not directly comparable on EBITDA margin.

**Related-party pricing.** ~65% of materials come from the promoters at "price lists in force and terms that would be available to third parties" (AR FY26); fees to them were 2.4% of revenue. We cannot test the prices from outside; the audit committee approves them annually.
**Other income is negligible** (₹4 cr in FY26, ₹5 cr in Q1FY27); earnings are almost entirely operating.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** The accounts are clean and simple, and cash conversion is good over time. The amber is for the size of the related-party flows (purchases, fees, leases) that set much of MSWIL's cost base: the margin minority shareholders see depends on prices agreed between related companies.

sections.title: Debt-free except leases; working capital jumped in FY26 with copper

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 MSWIL had ₹10 cr of bank debt and ₹223 cr of lease liabilities against ₹66-69 cr of cash: net debt ₹167 cr including leases, net cash ₹56 cr without them (company basis). By Jun-2026 bank debt rose to ₹61 cr and cash fell to ₹21 cr (net debt ₹40 cr before leases), as higher copper prices tied up money in stock and receivables. Inventory rose from ₹1,282 cr to ₹1,730 cr in FY26 and receivables from ₹1,244 cr to ₹1,884 cr; payables rose too (₹1,179 cr to ₹1,983 cr), and ₹1,108 cr of the payables are owed to the two JV partners, which therefore fund part of MSWIL's working capital.

The DCF gives ₹29, below the price, at a 12.2% cost of equity, 6% terminal growth and a 9.5% long-run margin: the market, like the house rule, is pricing either faster growth for longer or a lower cost of capital. **The BUY rests on the multiple returning towards MSWIL's own history, not on cash-flow value**; the honest caveat is that the history was built when margins were 11-13%.

sections.title: Our honest summary: India's harness leader at 24.1x Sep-28E EPS; BUY, but the case is the multiple

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** the incumbent wiring-harness supplier to most of India's best-selling cars, growing well ahead of car production, with ROCE near 40%, no debt beyond leases and a ~62% payout. You are also buying into a structure where the two promoters supply ~65% of the materials, take 2.4% of revenue in fees and decide which customers MSWIL serves, and where one customer takes 41% of output.

**What you are paying:** 33.7x our FY27E and 26.2x FY28E EPS for ~18% a year EPS growth (mostly margin recovery). Since listing the market has paid a median 41.8x forward for MSWIL; today it pays 26.2x, close to the lowest it has ever paid. The street's targets (median ₹49) sit between today's price and ours.

**We would move to HOLD above ~₹47.0** and to SELL above ~₹56.8 on today's numbers.

**This is a multiple call more than an earnings call.** Our EPS is below the street; our 38.5x is above the street's 30-35x because the house rule anchors on MSWIL's own 41.8x history. At the street's 35x our EPS still gives ₹49 (+45%), and even the bear case is above today's price; the DCF (₹29) is the one method that is not.
**Biggest swing factor:** the margin. Each 1x of multiple is ~₹1.41 a share; each point of EBITDA margin in FY28-29E moves the target by ~₹7.4.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Motherson Sumi Wiring India (standalone; no subsidiaries; Rs crore). One business (wiring harnesses and harness components for Indian vehicle makers), so revenue grows at a single rate and EBITDA margin is a driver; the business-line build (existing plants vs the three greenfields) is kept in lineBuild and checked against model revenue in MSUMI.ctx.js. Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: FY27: Q1 revenue Rs3,407 cr (+37%; ~7 points copper pass-through, the rest volume, content and new programmes); Q1 x4 is already +19%. We assume Rs3,550 cr in each of Q2 and Q3 and ~Rs3,600 cr in Q4 (growth falls to ~8% in Q4 against a Rs3,335 cr base that already carried copper and the greenfields). FY28-29: PV production +6-8% a year (after the GST-cut year), content per vehicle +4-5% (features, EV/hybrid share 8.5% of revenue in Q1FY27, 1.5-1.7x the content of an ICE car per JM Financial), greenfields reaching ~Rs2,000 cr a year; copper held at Q1FY27 levels (no further pass-through inflation).

lineBuild._why: Company disclosure: FY26 revenue Rs11,478 cr = existing plants Rs10,438 cr + greenfields Rs1,040 cr (Q4FY26 presentation p10). Greenfields ran at ~Rs443-450 cr a quarter in Q4FY26-Q1FY27 and are sized for ~Rs2,000 cr a year (Q4FY26 call). Existing plants are the balance.

assumptions._marginWhy: FY26 9.2% (11.4% excluding Rs127 cr of greenfield start-up losses); Q1FY27 7.6%. FY27: Q1 7.6%, then ~8.5% for Q2-Q4 as the 3-6 month copper lag unwinds (management: majority of customers on a three-month reset) and the greenfields move above breakeven, but the NCR minimum-wage increase (35-40%) is recovered only partly and slowly ('nobody can predict exactly the timeline'). FY28-29: greenfields at parity with old plants and some wage recovery; we stay well below the 11-13% of FY22-25 because copper pass-through at cost permanently inflates revenue (denominator effect, as the CFO said) and royalty, management fee and support fees to the two partners take ~2.4% of revenue.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex guided at ~Rs200 cr in FY27 (Q4FY26 call), funded internally; FY26 Rs201 cr. Management said in Aug-2026 that new expansion plans will follow 'in the next few quarters' as plants run at ~80%. We add ~Rs40 cr a year of new leased plant (right-of-use assets, most plants are leased from SAMIL) because the engine has no lease line, and lift capex to Rs270-280 cr in FY28-29 for the next round of plants.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs216 cr = 13.5% of average gross block (Rs1,604 cr), high because right-of-use (leased) buildings and harness tooling depreciate fast. Q1FY27 Rs60 cr.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied by the engine to net cash only (borrowings include Rs223 cr of lease liabilities, so there is no treasury income until net cash turns positive). Bank deposit yield ~6%.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Recurring items, not treasury: interest unwinding on security deposits with SAMIL and others (Rs2.7 cr in FY26, AR note 31), interest on deposits and small asset-sale gains. FY26 other income Rs3.9 cr (AR note 22; Rs12.8 cr in FY25 when cash was higher); Q1FY27 Rs5.4 cr. FY27E = Q1 plus ~Rs1.2 cr a quarter; Rs6 cr from FY28.
assumptions._interestWhy: Mostly interest on lease liabilities (Rs20.5 cr in FY26 incl. leases from SAMIL) plus working-capital lines: external debt rose from Rs10 cr (Mar-26) to Rs61 cr (Jun-26); Q1FY27 finance cost Rs8 cr.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Policy-like payout of ~62% of profit for FY26 (final Rs0.58 a share) and FY25; 59-65% since listing.

dcf._betaWhy: Tied to Indian car and truck production (cyclical) but net-debt-free with a 41% customer: beta 0.95, cost of equity 12.2%. Debt is only leases, so the cost of equity is the discount rate.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian vehicle production ~5-6% plus content growth; house range 5-6%: 6%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~13% in FY29E to 8%.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin held at ~9.5%: no return to the 11-13% of FY22-25 while copper is at today's price.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Asset-light assembler: capex ~1.7-2% of revenue in FY24-26; depreciation 1.8-1.9% of revenue.
